findings.title: The memory-budget tests accept the result of a solve that ignores the budget
findings.claim: L7 suite doc (Tests/ZTronLPLivenessTests/L3ToL10Tests.swift:186-188): 'the node pool respects the budget; exceeding it degrades (drops bases) and, if still exceeded, stops with .feasible(stoppedBy: .memoryBudget)'; test names sixteenMegabytesIsEnoughAndIsRespected (L3ToL10Tests.swift:190) and memoryBudgetDegradesThenStops (Tests/ZTronLPBranchAndBoundTests/BranchAndBoundTests.swift:241); HANDBOOK Testing 'The liveness rules of §12.2 each have a test'.
findings.observed: Both tests assert `status == .optimal || stopReason == .memoryBudget` (L3ToL10Tests.swift:198, BranchAndBoundTests.swift:246) and read no byte count, dropped-basis count or warning. On memoryBudgetDegradesThenStops' own instance and solver (randomMILP 12x60 seed 4242, BranchAndBound(nodeSelection: .bestBound, heuristics: .none)): 2,000 B -> noSolution(stoppedBy: memoryBudget) after 19 nodes; 4,096 B -> same after 29; 16 MiB -> optimal 593 (3191 nodes); no budget -> optimal 593 (3269 nodes). The unbudgeted result satisfies both assertions.
findings.whyWrong: A regression that stops enforcing the budget (or the degrade step in SearchTree.checkGapAndMemory) or undercounts openBytes turns the 2,000-byte case into .optimal, which the test accepts; the 16 MiB test cannot fail on a node pool that grows past 16 MiB; neither test checks degradation. Mitigation: aBudgetTooSmallForTheTreeStopsWithTheIncumbent (4,096 B, L3ToL10Tests.swift:202-215) and the L10 exit-path test require .memoryBudget, so a budget ignored entirely is still caught; a loosely honoured budget or a dead degrade step is not.
findings.repro: cd /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer/verification/probes/cycle-A && swift build -c release --product F7 && perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 300 .build/release/F7 membudget   (Slots/F7/Extra.swift memBudget)
findings.evidence: budget 2000: noSolution(stoppedBy: ZTronLPCore.StopReason.memoryBudget) nodes 19 | budget 4096: noSolution(stoppedBy: memoryBudget) nodes 29 | budget 16777216: optimal nodes 3191 objective 593.0 | budget nil (default): optimal nodes 3269 objective 593.0
findings.documented: No. README risk 4 and the 'Memory is budgeted, partly' bullet say what the budget counts, not that these tests leave it unchecked.

findings.title: Scripts/lint.sh misses violations inside its own stated C2/C3/C6 scope
findings.claim: Scripts/lint.sh:2-8 'CI runs this; it exits non-zero on the first rule that is broken ... C2 no global mutable variables in library code ... C3 every @unchecked Sendable is listed and must carry an // INVARIANT: comment ... C6 no DispatchSemaphore, Thread.sleep, blocking command-buffer wait or DispatchGroup wait'; HANDBOOK 'no global mutable state ... no blocking primitives'; SPEC v0.2 §2.2 'no new @unchecked Sendable (the count stays at one)'.
findings.observed: Mutation test on a copy of the script, one injected line per run. Not caught (rc=0): `@MainActor var counter = 0` in Sources; `commandBuffer.waitUntilScheduled()` (only waitUntilCompleted is listed); `sleep(1)` starting in column 0 (pattern '[^A-Za-z_.]sleep\(' needs a preceding character); `nanosleep(&ts, nil)`; any `@unchecked Sendable` without INVARIANT under Tests/ (code() greps Sources only). Caught: nonisolated(unsafe) in Sources and Tests, `var`/`public var` globals at column 0, every `static var x =`, @unchecked without INVARIANT in Sources, DispatchSemaphore/Thread.sleep/waitUntilCompleted/DispatchGroup/usleep(/indented sleep(.
findings.whyWrong: CI relies on this gate for C2/C3/C6, and these forms pass it. Mitigation: Swift 6 language mode (Package.swift:23) rejects nonisolated global vars, covering `public private(set) var` and indented globals inside #if that lint also misses, but not @MainActor globals or blocking calls. No current violation exists in Sources/ or Tests/, so the gap is latent.
findings.evidence: 'lint: all rules hold' with rc=0 for each uncaught mutation; rc=1 with the rule's message for each caught one

findings.title: Debug and Thread-Sanitizer runs report skipped MIPLIB cases as passed
findings.claim: README 'Building and testing': 546 tests pass in a debug build; README §5 'Thread Sanitizer: no reports on ... branch-and-bound, CP-SAT, ... integration ...' with the CI thread-sanitizer job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:65) as the gate.
findings.observed: CorpusTests.swift:125, :151, :171 `guard !Self.slow.contains(instance.name) || Slow.enabled else { return }`; Slow.enabled is false in any DEBUG build without ZTRONLP_SLOW_TESTS=1 (CorpusTests.swift:9-17). In debug, branchAndBoundWithBothStrategies runs 6 of 10 instances, cpSatClosesEveryPureIntegerInstance 3 of 7, cpSatWithoutTheLPPropagator 2 of 6; the other 12 cases return at their first line and count as passes (baseline 03: 'cpSatWithoutTheLPPropagator(_:) with 6 test cases passed after 7.784 seconds', no known issue; release 04 records the mod008 known issue after 60 s). The CI TSAN job and HANDBOOK's TSAN command are debug builds, so under Thread Sanitizer B&B never runs stein45, lseu, enigma or mod008, CPSAT() never runs stein45, lseu, mod008 or p0201, and CPSAT(lpPropagator: false) never runs stein45, lseu, enigma or mod008.
findings.whyWrong: Skipped cases are reported as passes in the 546-test count and in CI, and the TSAN claim on the integration target covers only the reduced corpus, without the longest parallel searches. Swift Testing's .enabled(if:), which the SATLIB tests use, would show them as skipped.

findings.claim: Test name (Tests/ZTronLPTestSupportTests/FixtureTests.swift:39) and comment 'Dual feasibility of the constructed pair'. Oracle 1 is the reference for every engine's duals.

findings.title: Manifest and HANDBOOK misstate the dependency and import graph
findings.claim: Package.swift:69-70 'The only two dependencies (§2): ... Heap / OrderedDictionary / BitSet'; Package.swift:159 gives ZTronLPCPSAT heap, orderedCollections, bitCollections; Package.swift:182 gives ZTronLPTestSupport ZTronLPNumerics; HANDBOOK.md:134-135 'branch and bound and CP-SAT are the two that import an LP engine'.
findings.observed: No file imports OrderedCollections or BitCollections. HeapModule is imported only by Sources/ZTronLPBranchAndBound/SearchTree.swift. ZTronLPCPSAT imports only Atomics, Foundation, Core, Numerics and Simplex. ZTronLPTestSupport imports Core, Dispatch and Foundation, not Numerics. ZTronLPInteriorPoint imports ZTronLPSimplex for crossover-lite, which makes it a third LP-engine consumer.
findings.whyWrong: Three declared products are dead dependencies for every client of ZTronLPCPSAT. The manifest comment and the HANDBOOK sentence describe a graph that is not the real one.

findings.title: Cancellation-latency figures count solves that finished before the cancel as 0 ms
findings.claim: README §5 / HANDBOOK 'Cancellation latency, 240 solves: p99 3.64 ms, worst 4.43 ms'; L1 test p99 bounds.
findings.observed: LivenessHarness.cancellationLatency records latency 0 when the solve returned before Task.cancel() (LivenessHarness.swift:45-48), and both the benchmark and the L1 test put those zeros into their quantiles. A probe on the benchmark's own instances, windows and seed gave Simplex(.primal) 30 interrupted / 8 finished first / 2 finished after the cancel; InteriorPoint 9 / 8 / 23; BranchAndBound 35 / 5 / 0. With 40 samples per row p99 = max, so the published per-row p99 and max are unaffected. p50 shifts (primal 0.16 -> 0.21 ms), and the all-engines p99 over 240 samples is taken at a slightly lower rank of the real latencies. Worst observed was 8.05 ms (IPM), within the 50 ms acceptance.
findings.whyWrong: A latency quantile that includes non-cancellations is optimistic. The measured effect on the published numbers is negligible.
findings.documented: The CancellationSample.finishedFirst doc describes the flag, but the benchmark and README do not say that zeros are included.

summary: Cycle A / F7: the gates, the 546-test count, the README §1 example, the §2 defaults and API shapes, the layering (no engine imports Metal; BLAS/LAPACK only through the shim), the netlib, transport and MIPLIB benchmark counts, deterministic B&B on nine MIPLIB instances, Oracle 1 (an independent KKT certificate on every suite) and TSAN on simplex/IPM/facade all hold. No critical or high defect was found. Nine findings: one medium (two memory-budget tests accept the result an unbudgeted solve gives, so they cannot catch a loosely honoured budget or a dead degrade step; only the 4,096-byte L7 test and L10 catch a budget ignored entirely), six low (README Hilbert warning counts wrong for orders 4-5; lint misses waitUntilScheduled, column-0 sleep(, nanosleep, @MainActor globals and anything under Tests/; debug and TSAN runs report skipped MIPLIB cases as passes; fetch-miplib.sh ignores ZTRONLP_CORPORA; the fixture complementarity test checks columns only; the manifest declares three never-imported collections products and the HANDBOOK misstates the LP-engine consumers), and two info (a stale 'never green' README statement; latency samples that count a solve that finished first as 0 ms, with negligible effect on the published p99). Checkpoint: verification/cycle-A/F7-integrity.md; probes in verification/probes/cycle-A/Slots/F7/.
